slides.headline: “Is it normal that I don’t finish *from sex alone?*”
slides.lead: The question people are too shy to ask. Swipe.

slides.headline: Yes. *It’s the experience of most women, not a minority.*
slides.body: If sex on its own has never quite got you there, you’re in the overwhelming, entirely normal majority.
slides.note: From intimova.ng: Why most women don’t orgasm during sex.

slides.headline: It reflects anatomy, *not a flaw in you or your relationship.*
slides.body: Sex on its own usually doesn’t give enough attention to where most women’s pleasure comes from. That’s how bodies are built.

slides.headline: Feeling safe, relaxed and present *matters enormously.*
slides.body: Stress and a racing mind are among the most common reasons pleasure feels out of reach.

slides.headline: Learn what you like. *Then say it.*
slides.body: Kindly and curiously, on your own first. What you learn solo, you can carry into time together: guide a hand, change position, add a toy.

slides.headline: You’re not broken, behind, *or unusual.*
